sections.content:
The 3rd SPACE also did nothing to the container (only the timer changed). So SPACE only worked once. Interesting.
New hypothesis: SPACE "pours" the purple from the frame into the container, but the amount poured depends on the tilt of the frame. When the frame is axis-aligned, pouring fills... hmm, but the first SPACE (axis-aligned) poured 5 rows.
Wait, maybe SPACE doesn't pour at all. Maybe SPACE "flips" the contents of the container? No, that's not it.
Let me think about it from a different angle. What if the white container is a "glass" and the purple block in the frame is a "block of ice / solid purple"? Goal: make the container match the legend (top white, bottom purple)? Currently it's top purple, bottom white.
Or, the legend shows the initial state of the container (top white, bottom purple)? No, the initial container was all white.
Hmm, wait. Let me re-verify: the legend (nodes 5, 9) is white 10x5 on top, purple 10x5 on the bottom. This is exactly the shape of the container 10x10 split into two 10x5 halves. So the legend is showing the target state of the container: top half white, bottom half purple.
Current container: top half purple, bottom half white. So I need to swap the halves. The first SPACE made it top purple / bottom white... wait, no! Let me re-verify. Initially the container was all white (rows 34-43). After the 1st SPACE: rows 34-38 became purple, rows 39-43 stayed white. So SPACE filled the top half with purple.
If the goal is top white / bottom purple, then SPACE filled the wrong half?! Unless the legend is showing the current state (top white, bottom purple = the initial container state before SPACE? No, initially it was all white).
Hmm, wait. Maybe the legend is a "palette": the two colors available. And the goal is to fill the container completely with purple (making it all purple). The first SPACE filled the top 5 rows. The 2nd/3rd SPACEs did nothing. Why?
Maybe SPACE pours purple from the frame, and the pour continues while... no, that's not it.
Let me reconsider: maybe SPACE only works when the frame is tilted (45°). The 1st SPACE was done when the frame was axis-aligned and it worked. Hmm, no.
Or maybe SPACE works once per "state change": the 2nd SPACE did nothing because the container was already in that state? That doesn't make sense either.
Let me try: tilt the frame with LEFT, then SPACE. Maybe tilting changes the pour amount / position.
